summary: A deque supports efficient insertion and removal at either end.
documentation: A deque supports efficient insertion and removal at either end. With maxlen set, appending to a full deque discards an item from the opposite end. Constructing one from a sequence retains the newest capacity items.
inputs: An object with events (list of JSON values) and capacity (integer 0..100).
returns: The retained events in arrival order.
caution: A bounded deque deliberately loses old entries and is inappropriate as the only audit log. A capacity of zero accepts input but retains nothing.
scenarios: Keep a short recent-message preview in memory.
Retain the latest local diagnostic events for a small status panel.
Maintain a rolling sample of recently observed values.
title: Keep a bounded recent history
problem: Input is {events, capacity}. Process events in arrival order and return only the most recent capacity events, still ordered oldest to newest within the retained window. Capacity zero returns [].
hint: Construct a deque with maxlen and convert it to a list.
goal: Use collections.deque(maxlen=...) or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
